heading: ### Round-18 gate/probe registry — routed-defect closure
notes: The round-19 coldread row's phrase ‘no legacy overrides’ is ambiguous. The wrapper defaults to the round-19 ledger and its selftest's no-historical-ledger-fallback case passes, but it still accepts --ledger-file/--ledger-rev/--inputs-overlay (measured --ledger-file run reported overrides_used=true). Unlike the round-20 selector, it does not refuse those flags. A reader could misread the phrase as flag refusal.

The round-18 dispositions manifest's supersedes field names .ufo/evidence/round-14/dispositions.json (and dispositions-before.json); the round-17 manifests also name round-14. Operationally, the round-17 dispositions manifest is no longer usable: the gate reports exit 2 / expected_input_digest_mismatch for it, while the round-18 manifest passes. Thus ‘round-17 manifests are superseded’ is true as an operational description, but not recorded as a direct round-18-to-round-17 supersedes pointer.
SentinelKillCode.md documents the adopted-orphan and same-tick-PID-reuse limits; the UID-change limit is in tools/registry-check.py's docstring, not that report.

defect-probes P11 reads the sibling kagi-shokunin repo relative to its fleet root. Running from a scratch clone outside the fleet sibling layout produced exit 2 (read-only kagi-shokunin source unavailable); running at the lane root with the fleet sibling present passed P11 and all 11 probes.

Out-of-section round-level observation: sources-census.sh validate exits 0, but census reports 142 tameshi rows at C0; base has 140 and C0 adds S281 and S282. This differs from the assignment's parenthetical ‘141 rows after this round's one new row’ and should be reconciled by L1.
